text:
kai: Fresh installer on my Win11 laptop. `redwoodctl auth login` says success but `redwoodctl localserve` returns 401.

sylvie: what path does the installer write to vs what CLI looks for?

kai: installer created C:\Users\kai\AppData\Local\Redwood\profiles\default\token.json but `redwoodctl config get profiles.path` returns C:\Users\kai\AppData\Roaming\redwoodctl\profiles. CLI isn't seeing it.

ops: classic APPDATA vs LOCALAPPDATA mismatch. Short-term: set REDWOOD_PROFILE_DIR to point at the installer path or create a junction: `mklink /J "%APPDATA%\redwoodctl\profiles" "%LOCALAPPDATA%\Redwood\profiles"`.

kai: set REDWOOD_PROFILE_DIR and restarted shell — localserve started picking up the token.

packaging: thanks for reporting. We'll patch the MSI; looks like the installer used the wrong constant. We'll open a tracked issue and schedule a canary. Also want to avoid changing existing tokens on upgrade.

sylvie: small related thing: headless login in CI printed the device URL then attempted to spawn `start`/`xdg-open` and returned a non-zero exit code in our container, causing the test harness to mark the job failed. If headless or non-interactive, the CLI should only print the URL and exit 0.

ops: filed CM-701: "headless login must not spawn platform opener in non-GUI/CI environments". Suggested detection: if not isatty or DISPLAY/XDG_SESSION_TYPE empty, skip opener. Add explicit `--no-open` flag too.

packaging: also noticed token schema drift during a manual migration: legacy token.json uses `expires_at` (unix seconds) while the new loader expects `expiry` (RFC3339). Add a compatibility shim to accept both and a migrate command `redwoodctl profiles migrate --from=legacy`.

sylvie: agree accept both keys for a deprecation window and print a one-time migration notice. Docs should include the REDWOOD_PROFILE_DIR env var and an example one-liner to copy files: `mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/redwoodctl/profiles" && cp -R "$HOME/Library/Application Support/Redwood/profiles/"* "$HOME/.config/redwoodctl/profiles/"`.

kai: can we also improve the CLI error when it can't read a profile? Right now localserve returns 403 with no guidance. Suggest error: "Cannot read profile at <path>. If this is a machine-wide install, run `redwoodctl auth login` as the installing user or set REDWOOD_PROFILE_DIR to a readable path."

ops: adding that to CM-702: "improve actionable error for unreadable profile paths". QA checklist: fresh install, upgrade, per-user vs machine-wide installs, headless CI flow, and token migration.

packaging: scheduling canary for MSI fix and the headless/login guard. Will coordinate with QA for validation. infra-bot: deploy installer/msi-fix -> windows-canary at 2026-04-14T04:00Z.

sylvie: I'll validate canary on both Intel and Apple Silicon VMs for mac pkg too — we have symmetric issues where pkg wrote to Library/Application Support while CLI defaults to XDG. We should detect installers and fallback locations for a couple releases to avoid breaking onboarding.

kai: thanks all. Happy to retest the canary and confirm release notes include the env var workaround and the migration hints.
